title: Open dense conical degeneracies for smooth Hermitian-matrix families on closed three-manifolds
source_title: Ubiquity of conical points in topological insulators
author: Alexis Drouot
difficulty_reason: Sard's theorem for two-by-two matrices does not directly give a global open dense statement for arbitrary Hermitian families on a three-manifold. The author proves stability through the discriminant and local spectral reductions, then recursively perturbs the two-dimensional spectral blocks over a finite chart cover while preserving the already treated regions. That global compatibility construction is the nonroutine obligation behind the stated density result.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem3 restricted to smooth compact boundaryless three-manifolds X and finite N≥2 Hermitian families, in the explicit C-infinity Frechet topology. Full openness and global finite-chart density construction retained, not merely Sard in the two-by-two case. Named elementary spectral continuity, Sard and bundle triviality on balls are standard prerequisites. The original PDF contains embedded draft-text duplicates in introductory figures on4–8; unchanged originals/native TeX retained and exact theorem7/core10–19 remain legible. Bounded display notes: positive discriminant is the explicitly supplied squared Vandermonde definition (first product misses the constant sign); trace identity2.4 prints2F2−2F1² but the same squared-gap construction is correctly given as2G2−G1² on19. These are finite algebraic normalization typos, and no stronger mathematical conclusion is inferred. Genericity is not a claim about differential-operator potentials, physical current asymptotics or the separately referenced Chern-number formula.
